notes:
A settings page that explains your own configuration, and a sidebar you can tidy from inside the app.

New: Settings, then Dashboards. Until now a `.dashboards.yml` either worked or
quietly did not, and there was no way to tell which from inside dashy. The new
page lists every dashboard it found, says where each one came from, and shows
what your config file is actually doing to it. A line that has no effect is
called out as having no effect, rather than left for you to infer from a sidebar
that looks wrong.

Hide the dashboards you never open. A folder you do not use no longer has to
hold a permanent slot in the sidebar. Hide and unhide from that same page, and
dashy writes the change into your config for you.

Config you can copy rather than compose. The page offers small ranked YAML
fragments for the common setups, so shaping a workspace no longer starts from a
blank file and a guess.

Three fixes worth naming:

Deleting a project folder no longer breaks the app. Removing a folder while
dashy was running used to make its pages fail outright. They now load, and they
say the folder is gone, where before they described it as merely empty, which
was not true and sent you looking in the wrong place.

Dropdowns are keyboard-usable again. Arrow-keying through a dropdown in Firefox
could submit on the very first keystroke and strand you on the first option, with
no way to reach the rest. Every dropdown that submits on change now waits for a
real choice.

Calendar rows can do what todo rows do. Ticking an item off and acting on it now
works from the calendar view, not only from the todo list.

Also in this release, though not visible on Windows: the in-app Claude chat
gained turn outcomes, a queue, and recovery from an interrupted answer. That
feature needs the Claude CLI, which this build does not carry, so it stays off
here.
